title: Initiative Hub: Operational Radar & Error Budget Passport
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: As Redwood scales Dedicated and Private deployments, teams need a single operational view that tracks per-service error budgets, current SLI health, and automated gating decisions. This initiative will deliver an "Error Budget Passport" concept surfaced in the Console (Operational Radar) that groups SLOs, shows burn rate, links the ledger and runbooks, and exposes automatic gating for rollouts and canaries.

Goals:
- Provide a single-pane Operational Radar in Console that lists teams/services with their active SLOs, current burn rate, time-to-breach, and recommended mitigation actions.
- Surface an Error Budget Passport per service: allocated budgets, recent incidents, owner, associated runbooks, and historical ledger with links to evals.
- Integrate automated gating hooks so Dedicated/Private rollout pipelines can query passport status and apply canary/rollback policies when budgets are breached.
- Expose program-level KPIs for PMs and Eng leads (total # services with breached budgets, mean time to recover, weekly burn rate trend).

SLI/SLO definitions (initial set):
- Request success rate (5xx + inference drop) — SLO target: 99.90% over 30d
- P95 serving latency (end-to-end) — SLO target: 300ms for hosted API, model-family-specific targets for Dedicated
- Embedding correctness/regression (synthetic eval pass rate) — SLO target: 98% across canonical prompts

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console Operational Radar view MVP showing list of services with SLOs and numeric burn rates, filterable by team, region, and model family.
2) Passport detail panel with ledger entries (chronological), linked runbooks, owner, and automated gating flag.
3) API endpoints for querying passport status (/v1/ops/passport/{service}) and a webhook for rollout systems to receive breach events.
4) Two-way linkage to existing SLI ingestion pipeline (ENG-3412) and dashboard templates in Grafana (dash-ops-passport).
5) Regression tests and an e2e canary that exercises gating on a staged Dedicated cluster.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We will initially limit SLI ingestion to the canonical metrics ingested by the current telemetry pipeline to reduce scope (latency, errors, synthetic evals). Extending to custom SLIs will be a follow-up.
- Automated gating will be opt-in per-service. Conservative defaults will only block broad rollouts; emergency rollbacks require manual confirmation.
- Passport UI uses a compact card layout to avoid Console clutter; expanded detail lives in a dedicated Passport panel.

Implementation milestones:

- 2026-03-05: API schema for passport and breach webhook merged (ENG-3412 dependent)
- 2026-03-18: Console MVP wireframes -> design review (DES-612)

- 2026-04-01: Staged canary and internal beta release

Metrics for success:
- % of critical services with passports created within 4 weeks of release > 70%
- Reduction in surprise SLO breaches during rollouts by 40% for teams that enable gating
- Time-to-detect SLO breaches improved by 25% (via consolidated radar)

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: internal alpha for platform + SRE teams, create passports for 10 high-priority services.
- Week 2: invite 3 pilot product teams (hosting, dedicated runtime) and enable opt-in gating.
- Week 4: iterate on UI and auto-scaling interactions based on pilot feedback; prepare broader beta announcement.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-automating rollouts could cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: opt-in gating + manual override + gradual defaults.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps may under-report burn rate. Mitigation: require instrumentation checklist before passport creation; surface data confidence level in passport.

Next steps:

- Design accessibility pass and small-card/expanded-card polish (owner: Marco)
- Coordinate with Eng telemetry to ensure metric coverage for first 10 services (owner: Priya)
